content:
Rule: Find the large object that encloses holes (0-regions unreachable from the border). Let k be the block scale — the unique k≥2 such that every other multi-cell object is an exact tiling of solid k×k blocks (k=2 in both training pairs, k=3 in the test, where all objects are 9×9/3×3). The output is (big-object height×k) × (width×k) filled with the big object's color; each connected hole component becomes one output object — every hole cell at local position (r,c) inside the big object is replaced by a solid k×k block of the matched object's color at (k·r, k·c). A hole component is matched to the object having exactly k²·(hole cells) cells and whose k×k-block downscale equals one of the 8 symmetries of the hole-component shape (verified on all 7 training objects; e.g. test: 7-cell component↔8-object, 6-cell↔5-object, T-shaped 5↔6-object, L-shaped 5↔9-object, singles↔3-blocks). Noise (colors appearing only as isolated single pixels, e.g. the 2s) is ignored, and acts as a wildcard inside object bboxes during tiling checks.

Verified mentally against both training pairs (reproduces the 12×12 all-2 output with 8/1/3 blocks, and the 28×20 all-3 output with 4/5/6/1/5 blocks) and applied to the test: 10×10 color-4 frame → 30×30 output, background 4, with block groups: color 8 at rows 3-11/cols 3-11 pattern, color 5 at rows 3-11/cols 18-26, color 3 at rows 12-14/cols 15-17, color 6 at rows 18-26/cols 3-11 area, color 9 at rows 18-26/cols 15-23 area, color 3 at rows 24-26/cols 24-26.
